description: Athlete asks to add strength training to their plan. Dean should give concrete guidance on how to integrate S&C — specific days, what to focus on, and how it fits around runs — without rewriting the whole plan.
inbound_sms: I want to start adding some strength training. Can you build that into my plan? Maybe 2x a week

user.name: Priya
user.experience_level: intermediate — running 3 years, 10k PR 48:00, second half marathon

ground_truth.expected_change: Add 2 strength sessions per week. They should be on easy run days or after easy runs — NOT before/after tempo or long run days. Focus areas should be relevant to running: glutes, hips, core, single-leg work.
ground_truth.change_scope: Ongoing integration into the plan going forward.
must_include: specific days recommended for strength (e.g. Monday and Thursday after easy runs)
what to focus on in the sessions (glutes, hips, core — runner-specific)
guidance that strength should not be done day before or day of hard quality sessions or long runs
must_not_include: vague advice like 'add some gym work' with no specifics
scheduling strength the day before tempo or long run
reducing running volume to accommodate strength without being asked
a full bodybuilding program — this is running-specific S&C
ground_truth.tradeoff_to_flag: First few weeks of strength training may cause DOMS — warn Priya to start light and expect some leg fatigue. Keep easy run paces easy.
ground_truth.notes: Strength training is a legitimate and valuable part of half marathon prep. Dean should enthusiastically support it, give specific day recommendations (easy run days make sense here: Mon/Thu), and outline what runner-relevant strength looks like. Keep it actionable — not a physiology lecture. The response can be slightly longer than a typical SMS since it's giving a new structure.
